answer: A farm that wants 181 keys therefore pays 181 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the saffron seed, the sable timing is verifiable from the yarrow record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 111 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is inexpensive once and expensive in bulk. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
